text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's parliamentary culture and media commission approved a draft coat of arms to replace the communist era crest of a lion and the red star.

The draft, which features two golden lions standing against the background of a red shield with a crowned lion, is expected to be approved by parliament on Thursday, putting to an end a seven-year row over the country's crest.

-- Bulgaria sees the forced assimilation of Bulgarian ethnic Turks by communist authorities in the 1980-s as one of the most shameful pages in its modern history, Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov told Turkish parliament.
Stoyanov, on a three-day official visit to the neighbouring contry, was the first Bulgarian head of state to appear before the Turkish legislative body.

-- Heads of Bulgarian criminal groupings, who are trying to influence local politicians, would be smashed, said Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev after a deputy claimed that members of parliament were dependent on the country's powerful strong-arm groupings.
-- Bulgaria's central bank said that the International Monetary Fund had disbursed on July 29 a $137 million loan instalment under a 14-month $510 standby agreement approved in April.
-- Bulgaria's monthly inflation is expected at about four percent in July and a bit lower in August, head of Bulgaria's Economic Institute Alexander Dimitrov said.

-- The Balkan neighbours Bulgaria and Turkey are to set up a joint military unit for peace-keeping operations in the region under a military agreement signed in Ankara by the two countries' army chiefs of staff.
